findings.description: The razor is drawn repeatedly across dry, unlathered chin, upper lip, cheeks, temple and forehead for the full 10 s, yet the stubble, skin and eyebrows show no change at any point — no hair removed, no lather displaced, no skin drag or reddening. The stroking action never produces its expected effect; the razor reads as hovering/miming rather than acting on the skin.

findings.invariant_violated: reflection must be simultaneous with its cause
findings.description: At 01:75 the real man's razor hand is raised to his temple/beside the eye, while the reflection shows the razor against the bridge of the nose with eyes closed and head lowered; at 04:25 the real razor is at the temple/brow while the reflection shows it at the eye/nose with face fully frontal. The reflected motion does not track the real motion that should cause it, as if the two were animated independently or out of phase.

findings.invariant_violated: effect-without-cause (reflected object with no real counterpart)
findings.description: At 09:00 the real man's right-hand fingers are pinched together near his jaw with no razor visible, while the reflection clearly shows a razor held against the cheek; at 09:25 the razor reappears in the real hand. The reflection depicts an action/object that the real scene is not producing.

The chin-up stroke sequence from 00:00-01:50 (razor at upper lip -> chin tilt -> stroke down jaw) recurs almost pose-for-pose at 05:00-07:25 and again around 08:50-09:50, with no progression in the task (no area completed, no rinse, no change in face). The action loops rather than advancing.

From 02:25 to 04:00 the razor is dragged repeatedly across the eyebrow and forehead (no stubble there), then the hand simply returns to the chin; the eyebrow and hairline are unchanged. The action is neither completed nor visibly interrupted and produces no effect.
